messages:
amy_sales: Folks, POC ask from VaultBank: BYOK with HSM KEKs (AWS CloudHSM + on-prem DR), monthly rotation, and proof Redwood never handles plaintext KEKs. They also want cost impact for hosted. Need a one-pager + simple runbook by EOD.

ravi_se: Quick Q: do they expect Redwood to call their KMS for wrap/unwrap, or require a KMIP proxy to an on-prem HSM?

amy_sales: They prefer KMS calls (CloudHSM) and an on-prem fallback via KMIP.

jordan_security: Security checklist: FIPS 140-2/3 attestation, HSM tamper reports, rotation logs, KMS principal ARNs, and audit event exports. Confirm we only store encrypted DEKs and key IDs.

mike_eng: We support envelope encryption. Flow: client generates DEK, wraps it with customer CMK (aws kms encrypt), sends wrapped DEK + payload. Redwood stores wrapped DEK; unwraps by calling customer KMS on-demand. Sample CLI: `aws kms encrypt --key-id <ARN> --plaintext dek.bin --ciphertext-blob dek.enc`.

laura_pm: Pricing: if keys remain in customer's KMS they bear HSM costs; Redwood charges per-proxy operation surcharge. If Redwood must manage HSM (dedicated custom key store), add fixed infra + hourly HSM costs. I'll draft two options.

ravi_se: Rotation note: customer rotates CMK; wrapped DEKs remain valid if KMS supports previous key versions. We'll run unwrap compatibility in POC. Recommend short DEK cache with TTL for perf but document tradeoffs.

jordan_security: Provide sample audit entry: `{"event":"kms.decrypt","key":"arn:...","actor":"redwood-proxy","ts":"2025-11-02T12:00:00Z"}` and offer log export to customer's S3.

infra-bot: infra: provisioned kmip-proxy-test-vaultbank (id: kmip-07) at 2025-11-02T09:12:31Z.

amy_sales: Perfect. Who can turn this into a one-page FAQ + 2-week POC runbook? Need it by EOD to send to VaultBank.

mike_eng: I'll assemble the runbook + minimal IAM policy snippet and drop links here shortly.

amy_sales: Thanks team! :thumbsup:
